headline: Balance two heaps and lazily discard expired values
statement: Return the median of every length-k window of nums. An odd window uses its middle ordered value; an even window uses the mean of its two middle values. Return medians in increasing window-start order.
constraints: Output accepts absolute error up to 0.00001.
intuition: Keep the current window's smaller and larger halves in two heaps. Balance their active sizes to expose the middle values. Removing a buried heap value is difficult, so mark it as expired and discard it when it reaches the top. Active counts must change immediately.
approach: Insert values into the appropriate half and rebalance their active sizes.
Mark the outgoing value in a delayed-count map and subtract it from its logical half.
Prune expired roots before moving values between heaps.
Read the lower root for odd k or average both roots for even k.
correctness: All active lower-half values are no greater than active upper-half values, and rebalancing keeps lower size equal to upper size or one larger. Lazy removals adjust logical sizes immediately; pruning ensures reported roots are active. These invariants identify the correct middle value or middle pair after every complete window.
bruteForce: Sort each window independently, taking O(nk log k). Maintaining a sorted Python list reduces comparison work but list insertion/removal still costs O(k) per slide.

complexity.explanation: Each entry is pushed and eventually popped at most once. Lazy expired entries can remain buried, so this version may retain O(n) entries rather than O(k).

pitfalls: Physical heap lengths include expired entries and cannot drive balancing.
Prune roots before using their values.
Duplicate values are interchangeable, but delayed removal counts must preserve occurrence count.
